2.text: and is called “windward room” (aiwaˊʟon). These names call to mind the

3.text: combinations of winds and points of the compass referred to previously.¹

4.text: Because of the position of the sleeping-room, the tent often has a some-

5.text: what oval shape, the rear bulging out under pressure of the poles used in the

6.text: construction of the inner room. The rear side (kɪˊnmen) of the sleeping-room

7.text: has a lamp fixed in the middle, quite near the wall (Plate XIV). Above it, near

8.text: the ceiling, a line is stretched, which serves for hanging up small articles of

9.text: dress that require drying over the lamp. The left side of the sleeping-room

10.text: is always occupied by the master and his wife, and is therefore also called

11.text: “master’s place;” while the right side is given up to the younger members

12.text: of the family, and, when necessary, to guests and strangers. The Chukchee

13.text: sleeping-room, however, affords little room for the stranger. A few extra

14.text: men crowd it considerably, and are compelled to sit crouching in the strangest

15.text: postures while eating or conversing. When there are a number of guests,

16.text: they can only thrust their heads in, and must keep the rest of their bodies

17.text: outside of the room, lying flat on their stomachs, and raising themselves up,

18.text: like so many seals, from under the tent-cover, which is fastened around their

19.text: shoulders. As these gatherings are usually accompanied by a common meal,

20.text: and trays of steaming meat and kettles of boiling tea are brought inside, the

21.text: temperature becomes quite unbearable. The guests strip to the waist, the

22.text: inmates even farther than this, and their naked bodies are flushed with heat

23.text: and covered with perspiration. The only way to improve the situation is to

24.text: lift up the front of the inner tent-cover for a while, and let in a wave of

25.text: fresh cold air, which almost instantly lowers the temperature several degrees,

26.text: and causes the moisture to condense in thick white clouds. Such changes

27.text: of temperature, which occur several times during the evening, are trying to

28.text: the most hardened constitution, and the natives often catch cold from the

29.text: sudden frosty draughts. After the visitors have departed, the temperature

30.text: quickly goes down, and the inmates must be careful not to let in any more

31.text: cold air. Therefore, after the evening meal, nobody is allowed to go outside;

32.text: and so, to satisfy the demands of nature, every person is supplied with a

33.text: special vessel (Fig. 96), which the mistress pushes with one hand out from

34.text: under the room cover, and empties

35.text: on a large slab of snow which lies near

36.text: at hand in the outer room.

38.text: Eskimo, sleep with their heads to the

39.text: entrance, reclining on the common pil-

40.text: low. They cover themselves with blan-

41.text: kets made of several heavy skins sewed

42.text: together, similar to those of the Eskimo. Each blanket serves for a whole family.
